setupSteps: Pick the version. *Standing:* feet hip-width, knees soft, back near a wall if you tend to rock. *Seated:* a firm upright chair with a back, feet flat, sit tall. A seat takes the legs out of the move and makes it harder to rock (coaching view, snippets). *No equipment:* bottles, rucksack or band in the same positions.
Floor. Non-slip mat on a flat spot; a folded towel beside you to set the weights on. Clear a 1.2 m wide space with nothing the elbows can hit.
Pick up the weights safely. Bend knees and hips, keep the back flat, lift them to your sides. Do not rock them up with the back.
Starting position. Arms hanging at the sides (or in front of the thighs), elbows slightly bent (about 10-30 degrees of bend per ExRx, snippet), not locked.

Grip and turn. Palms facing the thighs (neutral, thumbs forward) is the recommended first version for beginners. Palms down is the common standard (several guides, snippets); one guide suggests thumbs-up if palms-down feels poor (snippet). One coach argues the thumb should end slightly higher than the little finger (Stoppani, snippet, a coaching view). FitPlate default: thumbs forward, little turning.
Plane. Raise the arms about 20-30 degrees in front of the body line, not straight out to the side (scapular plane; several coaches and clinical tests use it, snippets).
Brace. Ribs down, glutes lightly tight, tummy tight, shoulders down and slightly back, chin level.
Choose the weight. The lightest weight that lets you do 12 slow reps with 3-4 in the tank (section 7). Many beginners need very little (a bottle is fine).
Camera. Phone in landscape at about chest height (110-130 cm, est.), 2.5-3 m away, filming the front of the body with both arms in frame.
Warm up 3-5 minutes (est.): march on the spot, arm circles, shoulder rolls, and one set of 8 reps with empty hands.

steps.title: Stand tall with the weights at your sides
steps.action: Stand with feet hip-width, weights hanging at your sides, thumbs forward.
steps.feel: Weight in both hands, whole foot on the floor.
steps.visualCheck: Front: shoulders level, arms by the sides. Side: ear, shoulder and hip in a line.

steps.title: Soften the elbows and brace
steps.action: Bend the elbows very slightly and hold that bend, then brace the tummy and press the shoulders down.
steps.feel: Shoulders low, away from the ears; tummy tight.
steps.visualCheck: Front: shoulder-to-ear gap clear; elbows very slightly bent.

steps.title: Start the raise with the elbows
steps.action: Lift the elbows out and slightly forward; the weights follow. Let the elbows lead the move (Experience Life, eatthis, snippets).
steps.feel: The side of the shoulder starting to work; no pull in the neck.
steps.visualCheck: Front: arms rise evenly; hands stay slightly below the elbows.

steps.title: Stop at shoulder height
steps.action: Stop when the elbows reach about shoulder height (hip-shoulder-elbow angle about 80-90 degrees, est.); do not go higher.
steps.feel: A tight side of the shoulder, no pinching.
steps.visualCheck: Front: elbows level with the shoulders; arms look like a loose "T"; shoulders not shrugged. Side: arms slightly in front of the body line.

steps.title: Lower slowly
steps.action: Lower the elbows back toward the body in a controlled way.
steps.feel: The side shoulder lengthening under control, no dropping.
steps.visualCheck: Front: both arms lower at the same speed along the same path.

steps.title: Reach the bottom with relaxed arms
steps.action: Let the weights come to the sides, then pause before the next rep. Do not bounce or let the weights hit the thighs.
steps.feel: A small pause with the arms hanging.
steps.visualCheck: Front: hip-shoulder-elbow angle back to about 25 degrees or less (est.).

steps.title: Repeat for 10-12 reps
steps.action: Repeat from step 3 with the same range each rep.
steps.breathing: Out on the lift, in on the lowering.
steps.visualCheck: Both arms follow the same path and height.

steps.title: Set the weights down safely
steps.action: Bend the knees and hips with a flat back and set the weights on the mat or towel with a 2-3 s count.
steps.visualCheck: Side: back flat; the only sound is a soft touch.

commonMistakes.title: Swinging the body (momentum)
commonMistakes.text: Swinging the body (momentum). Why: the work moves to the trunk and upper trapezius, and a heavy weight is the usual cause (Peloton, Yahoo/AOL and T3 snippets). Fix: lighter weight, seated or back near a wall, 3 s lowering.

commonMistakes.title: Shrugging
commonMistakes.text: Shrugging. Why: the upper trapezius takes over from the side shoulder (several snippets; the Coratella study shows upper trapezius activity changes with arm rotation). Fix: shoulders down, think "elbows out, shoulders away from the ears".

commonMistakes.title: Raising above shoulder height
commonMistakes.text: Raising above shoulder height. Why: sources warn against elbows well above shoulder level (several snippets), and Kolber et al. linked it with impingement signs. Fix: stop when the elbows reach shoulder height.

commonMistakes.title: Hands higher than the elbows ("pouring a jug")
commonMistakes.text: Hands higher than the elbows ("pouring a jug"). Why: turns the arm inward and loads the upper trapezius and front of the shoulder (Coratella, Stoppani, snippets). Fix: thumbs forward and let the elbows lead.

commonMistakes.title: Locking the elbows straight
commonMistakes.text: Locking the elbows straight. Why: jolts the elbow and lengthens the load lever. Fix: keep a slight bend (10-30 deg per ExRx) throughout.

commonMistakes.title: Raising straight sideways with force, with a locked or jammed shoulder
commonMistakes.text: Raising straight sideways with force, with a locked or jammed shoulder. Why: coaches prefer the scapular plane, about 20-30 degrees in front, for comfort (snippets; a clinical test uses it with thumbs up to reduce pain). Fix: raise a little in front of the body.

commonMistakes.title: Weight too heavy
commonMistakes.text: Weight too heavy. Why: causes most of the above. Fix: choose by 3-4 reps in reserve (section 7); a bottle is a normal starting weight.

commonMistakes.title: Dropping the weights fast
commonMistakes.text: Dropping the weights fast. Why: loses half the work and jerks the shoulder. Fix: 3 s down.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. Why: raises blood pressure and brings dizziness (PubMed 7741618, carried). Fix: out on the lift, in on the lowering.

commonMistakes.title: Dropping dumbbells on the floor
commonMistakes.text: Dropping dumbbells on the floor. Why: noise for neighbours below and risk to feet. Fix: lower with a 2-3 s count onto a mat.

safetyNotes: Shoulder problems (impingement, rotator cuff, instability): Kolber et al. linked lateral raises above 90 degrees with impingement signs in weight trainers (snippet; association only). A fluoroscopy study found the subacromial space narrowest at lower elevation angles (snippet), so stopping at shoulder height does not remove the risk. Use thumbs forward, the scapular plane, a pain-free range, and stop if you feel pinching or pain in the shoulder; ask a physiotherapist. Harvard Health's impingement page (snippet) lists rest and physio as first-line care.

High blood pressure and heart disease: breathe out on the lift, never hold the breath, very light weight; arms above the heart raise blood-pressure load (coaching view, not sourced); get clearance first with heart disease or uncontrolled blood pressure.
Lower back problems: use the seated version or stand with the back near a wall, no leaning or rocking.
Neck pain or trapezius tension: shrugging overloads the neck; use very light weight and a short range.
Osteoporosis: loaded strength work is generally recommended; the raise itself loads the spine very little if the trunk stays still; with a vertebral fracture or severe osteoporosis ask a clinician.

Pregnancy and postpartum: a light seated raise is generally treated as low risk in uncomplicated pregnancy (PMC11193983 resistance training in pregnancy, carried; snippet), but ask your obstetrician, midwife or women's health physiotherapist; stop with dizziness, headache, pain, leaking or pelvic heaviness. ACOG's own wording: Not found.
Mumbai flat: mat under your feet, set the weights down gently, no glass bottles, keep clear of furniture, fans, windows and the balcony, and do not swing a rucksack near people.
